Key Personalities Associated with A&N Islands

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Focuses on important historical and key personalities associated with the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
Provides a one-line quick facts compendium designed for swift revision.
Summarizes essential revision points critical for competitive exam preparation.

cells: British naval officer who surveyed the islands in the 1780s; Port Blair is named after him
Most famous political prisoner of Cellular Jail (imprisoned from 1911); Port Blair's airport is named Veer Savarkar International Airport
Hoisted the Tricolour at Port Blair on 30 December 1943; renamed Andaman 'Shaheed Dweep' and Nicobar 'Swaraj Dweep'
Revolutionary imprisoned in Cellular Jail alongside other freedom fighters
First Lieutenant Governor of A&N Islands (1982–85), after the post was upgraded from Chief Commissioner
Current (2026) Lieutenant Governor of A&N Islands, in office since October 2017; former Chief of the Naval Staff
Current (since 2024) Lok Sabha MP from A&N Islands (BJP)
Not specific to A&N — candidates should avoid confusing national personalities with UT-specific ones in this chapter

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Distinguish carefully between the historical 'Chief Commissioner' era (pre-1982) and the 'Lieutenant Governor' era (1982 onward, starting with M.L. Kampani) — the post's designation change is occasionally tested.

items: Total islands: 836 | Inhabited: ~38 | Area: 8,249 sq km | Coastline: ~1,962 km.
Capital: Port Blair | Districts: 3 (South Andaman, North & Middle Andaman, Nicobar).
10° Channel separates Andaman & Nicobar groups; Great Channel separates Great Nicobar from Sumatra.
Highest point: Saddle Peak (732 m); Southernmost point of India: Indira Point, Great Nicobar.
Only active volcano in India: Barren Island; dormant volcano: Narcondam Island.
Seismic Zone V; struck by the 26 Dec 2004 Sumatra-Andaman earthquake & tsunami.
First British settlement: 1789, Chatham Island (Lt. Archibald Blair).
Cellular Jail: built 1896–1906; 7 wings, 693 cells, 3 wings survive; National Memorial since 1979.
Japanese occupation: March 1942 – October 1945 (only Indian territory occupied in WWII).
Netaji hoisted the Tricolour at Port Blair: 30 December 1943.
2018: Ross → Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Dweep; Neil → Shaheed Dweep; Havelock → Swaraj Dweep.
No Legislative Assembly; administered by an LG under the President of India.
Current LG: Admiral D.K. Joshi (Retd.), since October 2017.
1 Lok Sabha seat, 0 Rajya Sabha seats; judiciary under Calcutta High Court (Circuit Bench, Port Blair).
Andaman & Nicobar Command (ANC), HQ Port Blair — India's only tri-service unified command (est. 2001).
~30% of India's total EEZ lies around A&N Islands.
Great Nicobar Island Development Project: ~₹72,000 crore — ICTT (Galathea Bay), airport, township, power plant.
CANI submarine cable (2020) brought broadband to 10 major islands.
6 tribes: Great Andamanese, Onge, Jarawa, Sentinelese, Nicobarese, Shompen.
5 of 6 are PVTGs — only Nicobarese are not.
North Sentinel Island: entry illegal; Sentinelese totally uncontacted (John Allen Chau case, 2018).
Jarawa Policy 2004 + 2012 ANPATR amendment ban 'human safaris' on the Andaman Trunk Road.
9 National Parks, 96 Wildlife Sanctuaries (highest of any Indian state/UT), 2 Biosphere Reserves.
~86% forest cover — among the highest of any Indian state/UT.
Narcondam Hornbill: endemic to Narcondam Island only.
Galathea Bay, Great Nicobar: key Giant Leatherback Turtle nesting site, now overlapping the Great Nicobar Project.
Questions frequently test prominent personalities and freedom fighters linked to the Cellular Jail and A&N Islands.
One-line quick facts are directly tested in objective-type general knowledge questions.
Radhanagar Beach (Swaraj Dweep/Havelock): TIME magazine's 'Asia's Best Beach' (2004).
Ross & Smith Islands (Diglipur): connected by a natural sandbar at low tide.
Veer Savarkar International Airport, Port Blair — main air gateway.
Revise this chapter last — it consolidates every numeric/name fact from Chapters 1–9 in one place for rapid recall.
Cross-check the PVTG count (5 of 6 tribes) and the sanctuary count (96) — these are the two most frequently mis-remembered numbers.
Always verify current officeholders (LG, MP) closer to your exam date, since these can change.
